verdict_note: Based on reading only: no build and no tests were run. The Folio half is sound. The record, the enumerations and the stated bounds match STU-TYP-155..161, 133 and 192, and the empty-story form of lead decision (a) holds (see answers). Each of the six mutating rows is one snapshot undo step named by its catalog id, and refusals are typed. The defects are in the PDF export and in how the new records meet the old ones. F1 (high): the export now cuts a span at every local override and script run, and every span repeats the full resolved feature map. Type refuses a paragraph request with more than 32 styles or more than 64 features (text::limits), so ordinary documents make every layout.export_pdf refuse text_shaping_refused, while the command that caused it reported success. F2: all caps corrupts the PDF text layer of unrelated text: ToUnicode is keyed by glyph id and takes the first, lowercase, source. The builder's own run showed this, and the test was changed to compare glyph ids instead. F3: size, leading and tracking now have two storages on a style, and a paragraph style's record size beats a character style's legacy size, against STU-TYP-201. F4: a feature the font lacks is dropped silently, although Type returns an UnavailableInert receipt. F5: tracking is added per glyph, which displaces combining marks. F6: clear_overrides deletes hyperlinks. F8: export and read work is unbounded over overrides and based_on depth. F7 and F9 to F15 are low.

findings.certainty: READ (Type's request limits, the export's span cuts and feature emission); not run. The counts in the scenario follow from validate.rs:124 and :204.
findings.severity: high (a successful command leaves every PDF export of the document refused)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/layout_export.rs:532 (shape_paragraph sends text::limits()); crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/text.rs:305-324 (styles 32, features 64, font_resources 32 per request); crates/hsk-studio-type/src/validate.rs:124 (styles > l.styles is Budget) and :204 (sum of the styles' features > l.features is Budget); layout_export.rs:454-460 (every span carries its whole resolved feature map plus the kerning, capitalization and position projections); layout_export.rs:590-600 (spans are cut at every character range, every local override of the story and every script run); crates/hsk-studio-folio/src/typestyle.rs:419 (MAX_RECORD_FEATURES 256)
findings.what: Before the lane the export cut spans only at character ranges and sent no features. Now every local override and every script run adds cuts, and each span repeats the full resolved feature map. That map includes a paragraph style's map, so it is repeated on every span of the paragraph. Type refuses a paragraph request with more than 32 styles (32 font candidates) or more than 64 features in total. The export maps the refusal to text_shaping_refused for the whole document. Overrides that do not affect shaping still cut spans: underline, strikethrough, hyperlink, faux_bold and no_break, which are all reported as not rendered. Folio and the command accept up to 256 feature tags per record, so one such record (65 tags or more) can never export. The editor preview does not shape with these attributes, so nothing warns the user before export.
findings.scenario: 1. A paragraph style states opentype_features {onum, pnum, liga, calt, kern} (5 tags). One paragraph holds 7 hyperlinked words (7 local overrides), which makes 15 spans and 75 features. layout.export_pdf refuses text_shaping_refused (Budget). 2. Without any feature map, 16 underlined words in one paragraph make 33 spans, and the export refuses. 3. layout.set_character_attributes with 65 opentype_features tags succeeds; every later export refuses.
findings.fix: Merge adjacent spans whose shaping inputs are equal (font, size, script, language, feature map, case mapping, extra advance, baseline shift) before shaping, so fields Type does not read never cut a span. Give the layout export its own Type limits, sized to what the lane admits per paragraph (features up to MAX_RECORD_FEATURES per span, styles up to the merged span count, under an explicit bound), or bound MAX_RECORD_FEATURES by what one span can shape and refuse typed at set time. When a paragraph still exceeds the bound, refuse with a code that names the story and paragraph, not a bare Budget. Lead question 1.
findings.test: layout_character_attributes.rs, new test a_paragraph_with_many_overrides_and_a_feature_map_exports: a paragraph style with 5 feature tags; 20 single-word hyperlink or underline overrides in one paragraph; 40 tracking overrides of distinct values in another. Both export with lines > 0 and the expected host_loss counts. A record with 65 tags is refused typed at set time, or exports.

findings.certainty: READ, and the builder's own log: smb-type-character-attributes-1-focused-51b4d006.log:35119-35120. At 51b4d006 the text-layer assertion failed, and the page text read the stored lowercase source for the all-caps span.
findings.severity: medium (silent corruption of the PDF text layer of text the user never changed; search, copy and accessibility)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/layout_export.rs:374-389 (case_mapped: only the shaped copy changes) and :452-453; crates/hsk-studio-interop-layout/src/pdf_export.rs:935-944 (/ToUnicode keyed by glyph id; or_insert_with keeps the FIRST cluster's stored text); crates/hsk-studio-harness/tests/layout_character_attributes.rs:63-75 and :194-201 (the test compares glyph ids, not extracted text)
findings.what: All caps and lower case change only the copy that Type shapes. The PDF's /ToUnicode maps each glyph id to the stored text of the first cluster drawn with it. A capital glyph first drawn for a stored lowercase letter maps to that lowercase letter for the whole document. Every later capital drawn with the same glyph, in any story, extracts as lowercase. host_loss reports nothing. At 51b4d006 the PDF test asserted the text layer and failed. The tip's test compares glyph ids instead, so no test now covers the text layer.
findings.scenario: The test's own text 'Hello HELLO world of type', with capitalization all_caps on bytes 0..5. 'Hello' is drawn first, so the capital glyphs E, L and O get /ToUnicode 'e', 'l' and 'o'. The stored 'HELLO' at 6..11 then extracts as 'Hello', and a PDF search for 'HELLO' finds nothing.
findings.fix: Take the /ToUnicode text of a case-mapped cluster from the mapped characters, so a capital glyph always maps to a capital and no glyph id has two meanings. If the stored case must be recoverable, add /ActualText with the stored text for case-mapped spans (lead question 3). Until then, report host_loss case_transform_text_layer_approximated with a span count. Lower case is the same.
findings.test: In the_pdf_shapes_with_the_attributes_and_reports_what_it_does_not_draw, also extract the page text: bytes 6..11 read 'HELLO'. Bytes 0..5 read 'HELLO', or 'Hello' through ActualText, as ruled.

findings.severity: medium (STU-TYP-201 order broken across the two storages; the read reports a different size and leading than the PDF draws)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-folio/src/typestyle.rs:125-136 (StudioTypeStyle.font_size, line_height, letter_spacing) beside the lane's style_character size, leading and tracking (StudioTypeStyleRecords.style_character); crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/layout_ui/styles.rs:196-200 (layout.style.edit_style font_size_pt and leading_pt write the legacy fields); layout_export.rs:610 (size = attributes.size.or(cs).or(para_size)); layout_export.rs:847 (line height reads only the record's leading); layout_ui.rs:1415-1475 (layout.character_attributes reads only the record)
findings.what: The lane adds a second storage for size, leading and tracking on styles. The export takes the record's size first, whatever level it comes from. A paragraph style's record size therefore beats a character style's legacy font_size_pt, although STU-TYP-201 says the character style wins. The leading_pt that edit_style writes is ignored by the PDF, while the record's leading is drawn. The read reports size and leading as null for text sized through edit_style, but the PDF draws it at that size (STU-TYP-112: the full resolved record). Unset fields read null rather than the spec default (tracking 0, scales 100, shift 0), and the harness test pins that null.
findings.scenario: 1. layout.style.set_character_attributes gives the paragraph style Body the record size 10. layout.style.edit_style gives the character style Big font_size_pt 18. Big is applied to one word. The PDF draws the word at 10 pt, and layout.character_attributes reports size 10. 2. layout.style.edit_style Body with leading_pt 30: the PDF line pitch stays at 1.25 em.
findings.fix: Keep one storage per attribute (lead question 2). Either edit_style writes the style's record, and the legacy fields are folded into the record at the same level on open; or the resolver folds each style's legacy fields into that style's record before the next level overlays it. Both the export and the read use that one resolver. Unset fields read the declared spec default, marked as a default.
findings.test: layout_character_attributes.rs a_character_style_size_beats_a_paragraph_style_size_in_either_storage: (Body record size 10, Big legacy 18) gives a glyph size of 18 in the PDF and size 18 in the read; edit_style leading_pt 30 gives a 30 pt line pitch.

findings.certainty: READ (the export never reads Type's feature receipts); not run. UNVERIFIED: that the bundled Ubuntu-Light lacks smcp (D5).
findings.severity: medium (stored attributes not drawn and not reported; STU-TYP-158 'MUST report which path it took')
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/layout_export.rs:286-330 (capitalization and OpenType position become requests for smcp, c2sc, sups, subs, numr, dnom); layout_export.rs:533-560 (the prepared result's feature receipts are never read); layout_export.rs:959 (host_loss lists only character_of's fixed field list); crates/hsk-studio-type/src/engine.rs:401-418 (one FeatureState::UnavailableInert receipt per requested feature the font lacks); layout_export.rs:374-389 (case_mapped keeps a character whose case form is not one character of the same UTF-8 length, and is language-insensitive)
findings.what: When the font lacks a feature, Type shapes the run unchanged and returns an UnavailableInert receipt, which the export ignores. Small caps, all small caps, OpenType super- and subscript, numerator, denominator, and any opentype_features tag the font does not have are drawn as plain text with no loss line. All caps also leaves characters such as U+00DF and U+0149 lowercase without a report, and maps i to I under a Turkish applied_language. The lane notes cut synthesis, but the cut is not visible to the caller.
findings.scenario: capitalization small_caps on one word in a font without smcp: the PDF draws plain lowercase, and host_loss has no capitalization entry. A record with opentype_features {ss07: 1} in a font without ss07 is drawn plainly, with no loss. 'Strasse' spelled with U+00DF in all caps is drawn with a lowercase U+00DF, with no loss.
findings.fix: Read each paragraph's feature receipts. Report character_attribute_not_rendered for capitalization or position when its projected tag is inert, and opentype_feature_unavailable (element = the tag, with a count) for record tags. Count the characters case mapping could not map (case_mapping_incomplete). Synthesis per the STU-TYP-158 table stays a named gap.
findings.test: Use a font fixture without smcp. small_caps gives a host_loss capitalization count of 1; {ss07: 1} gives opentype_feature_unavailable ss07; all caps over U+00DF gives a case loss of 1.

findings.certainty: READ; not run. The mark displacement assumes Type returns a separate zero-advance mark glyph for the cluster, so the test uses a base with no precomposed form.
findings.severity: medium (misplaced combining marks and doubled tracking for every multi-glyph cluster; /W disagrees with the embedded font)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/layout_export.rs:540-551 (extra_advance_pt is added to every glyph whose cluster starts in the span, marks included); crates/hsk-studio-interop-layout/src/pdf_export.rs:931-934 (/W takes the first occurrence's layout advance, now including tracking) and :1064-1065 (glyph x = pen + x_offset; the pen moves by the layout advance)
findings.what: Type gives every glyph of a cluster that cluster's source range. A base and its combining mark both get the extra advance. The mark has zero advance and an offset measured from the pen after the base, so the widened base advance moves it `extra` to the right of its base, and the cluster gets twice the tracking. Arabic clusters with harakat and other multi-glyph clusters behave the same way. A glyph id's /W width becomes its first occurrence's tracked advance, so /W no longer matches the embedded font's widths. That affects extraction spacing and preflight width checks (UNVERIFIED whether check_pdfx4 flags it).
findings.scenario: 'x' + U+0301 + 'y' with tracking 500 at 12 pt. The x glyph and the mark each gain 6 pt, so the acute is drawn 6 pt to the right of the x, and y starts 12 pt later instead of 6 pt.
findings.fix: Add the extra advance once per cluster, on the cluster's last glyph in logical order, and skip zero-advance glyphs. Write /W from the untracked advance (Type's x_advance_pt), not the composed advance.
findings.test: layout_character_attributes.rs: export 'x' + U+0301 + 'y' with tracking 500. The mark's drawn x lies within [x_base, x_base + untracked advance of x]; y's x equals the untracked widths plus 2 x 6 pt; the /W entry of the x glyph equals its hmtx width.

findings.severity: medium (V4-02: hostile records make export and the read do unbounded work, with no cancellation check)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-folio/src/typestyle.rs:1168-1192 (chain_character: each call walks up to 4096 styles with chain.contains (linear) and linear style() and style_character() lookups; resolved_character scans every override linearly); crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/layout_export.rs:604-612 (two chain walks and one override scan per span); layout_export.rs:374-389 (case_mapped: spans.iter().find per character, before Type's size limits apply); crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/layout_ui.rs:1415-1475 and :1393-1408 (the read does the same per segment; mixed() compares each segment's value with every distinct value, for 44 fields)
findings.what: A valid layout_records entry with 65,536 one-byte overrides in a 1 MiB story makes plan_story run about 65,536 x 65,536 override scans (4.3e9 id compares), and case_mapped run up to 1M x 65,536 lookups, before Type's 32-style refusal is reached. A 4096-deep based_on chain costs about 5e7 steps per resolved_character call, and there are two calls per span. The read over the same story is O(segments x distinct values x 44), and each segment holds a full JSON copy of its record. Neither plan_story nor the read checks the cancellation token.
findings.scenario: Open a package whose layout_records holds such a story and run layout.export_pdf or layout.character_attributes over the story. The command runs for minutes, and the export job cannot be canceled while it plans.
findings.fix: Per export, index the overrides by story (a sorted list walked with the cuts) and memoize chain_character per style id. Walk the spans in order in case_mapped. Check cancellation per paragraph and charge a step budget (typed budget_exceeded). In the read, key the distinct values in a map and cap the segment count.
findings.test: V4-02 aggregate_over_budget-style tests: 65,536 overrides export within a step bound or refuse typed; the read over 65,536 segments is bounded; a 4096-deep based_on chain is bounded; a pre-canceled token stops plan_story.

findings.severity: low (hostile or stale override spans are accepted at open and fail later, far from their cause)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-folio/src/typestyle.rs:1465-1480 (overrides are checked only for order and overlap; the Folio records validator has no stories); crates/hsk-studio-session/src/layout_records.rs:161 (LayoutRecords::validate has the stories but does not cross-check the overrides); crates/hsk-studio-layout/src/textflow.rs:46-56 (map_pos uses checked_add) and :323-331
findings.what: An override may name a story the records do not hold, end past the story's byte length, or split a UTF-8 character. All three open. Bounds inside a character later refuse the whole PDF export (Type's range check: text_shaping_refused InvalidInput). An override whose end is near u64::MAX makes every text edit of its story fail (map_pos overflow, budget_exceeded). Records of a deleted story stay forever (class C, named for SMB-LAYOUT-DELETE-CASCADE-1, whose lane notes leave the LayoutRecords::validate story-id guard open).
findings.scenario: A package with an override {text_id S, start 1, end 2} on a story whose byte 0 starts a 2-byte character opens; layout.export_pdf then refuses text_shaping_refused.
findings.fix: In LayoutRecords::validate, check every override: text_id is a stored story (DanglingReference); end <= byte_len; start and end lie on char boundaries of inline text (InvalidField). Apply the same story-id check to paragraph_composition.text_id (the guard the cascade lane left open). See the rebase note.
findings.test: Session layout_records tests: the three hostile entries are refused at open with typed codes.

findings.severity: low (V4-06 sweep misses whole-content story writers)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-layout/src/alternate.rs:430-439 (update_linked_stories replaces a child story's content whole; the child's overrides go stale, the parent's are not copied, and linked_story_fingerprint ignores overrides; no host caller yet); crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/layout_ui.rs:928-932 (the egui test-host story editor's 'Commit text' replaces [0, len): every override maps to [0, 0) and is dropped, and every character range collapses into the last one); crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/text.rs:111-116, interop-layout idml_longdoc.rs:1113, interop-fig-native native.rs:3659, interop-vector-core ai_import.rs:1101 (they accept StudioTypeStyleRecords that may now carry the new fields, which their hosts neither read nor move)
findings.what: The class A regex (replace_story_text|shift_paragraph_records|shift_flow_records) matches only paths that edit a span of text. Writers that replace the whole content do not match, and they are not listed in notes.v4_06_sweep.
findings.scenario: In the test-host story editor, change one word of a story that has an override on another word and press Commit text: the override is gone.
findings.fix: List these sites in notes.v4_06_sweep with fixed or not applicable. The story editor should commit one replace of the changed middle (common prefix and suffix), so untouched overrides survive. update_linked_stories copies the parent's overrides under the child's id and includes them in the fingerprint.
findings.test: viewer_layout_ui.rs: committing a one-word change keeps an override elsewhere in the story.

findings.certainty: READ (textflow.rs:113-127 splits after every ends_paragraph character; U+000D and U+000A each end a paragraph, sentinels.rs:6-9)
findings.severity: low (a pasted CR LF makes an extra blank paragraph per line)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-layout/src/textflow.rs:113-127 and :148-161 (the empty-story paths the lane opened); crates/hsk-studio-layout/src/sentinels.rs:62-64 (Type's ends_paragraph)
findings.what: CR and LF each end a paragraph, so 'one' + CR LF + 'two' typed or pasted into a frame becomes three paragraphs: 'one' + CR, a paragraph holding only LF (drawn as a blank line), and 'two'. A non-empty story already split this way. The lane extends it to the empty frame, which before kept one paragraph and drew a line break.
findings.scenario: layout.replace_text with 'one' + CR LF + 'two' into a new frame gives 3 paragraphs, and the PDF has a blank line between the two lines.
findings.fix: Lead question 5: treat CR LF as one terminator in Type's ends_paragraph and layout's partition (UAX #29 GB3), or normalize CR LF to LF at the replace_text boundary.
findings.test: empty_story_edits.rs: 'one' + CR LF + 'two' gives 2 paragraphs, [0, 5) and [5, 8).

findings.severity: low (spec conformance of the model-facing surface)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/layout_ui.rs:1458-1470 (parameter rows); crates/hsk-studio-folio/src/typestyle.rs:790-818 (CHARACTER_PARAMS), :881-940 (validate: size, leading and scales must be > 0), :757 (opentype_features: BTreeMap<String, u32>); layout_ui.rs:1286-1309 (cleared accepts top-level fields and opentype_features/<tag> only); layout_ui.rs:1249-1257 (byte_span refuses start == end)
findings.what: (a) STU-TYP-221 asks for the three step values of STU-TYP-109 next to the seven fields; the rows have none, and UNKNOWN is emitted as JSON null, not an explicit UNKNOWN. (b) The rows give hard_min null for size, leading and the two scales, but the validator refuses values <= 0, so a model cannot discover that domain without trial and error. (c) STU-TYP-170 says a binary feature is stored as a boolean; {liga: true} is a decode refusal, and Folio cannot tell a binary 1 from alternate index 1. (d) STU-TYP-159 stores decoration fields separately, but one cannot be cleared on its own: 'underline/tint' is refused as unknown_character_attribute (STU-TYP-112). (e) layout.character_attributes cannot be read at an insertion point (start == end is refused).
findings.scenario: A model reads parameters, sees size hard_min null, sets size 0, and is refused folio_invalid_field.
findings.fix: Add step, coarse_step and fine_step to the rows (UNKNOWN where none is declared, plus the implementation's recorded choice per STU-TYP-109), and emit 'UNKNOWN' or document null as UNKNOWN in the row text. Add exclusive_min 0 (or a domain field) for size, leading and the scales. Accept true/false for binary tags (or rule it, lead question 4). Accept '<record>/<field>' in clear for decoration records. Allow start == end to read the attributes in force at a position.
findings.test: layout_character_attributes.rs: the parameter rows carry steps and the size domain; {liga: true} round-trips or is refused per the ruling; clear 'underline/tint' unsets only the tint; a read at 3..3 returns one segment.

findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-folio/src/typestyle.rs:935 (a Node target checks only label(node_id)); crates/hsk-studio-folio/tests/character_attributes.rs (accepts an SPGS id that the document does not hold)

findings.test: layout_character_attributes.rs: a node hyperlink to an unknown id is refused typed; one to an existing page spread is accepted.

findings.certainty: READ the logs and git diff e2f70907 83cb89b8 -- tests
findings.where: Handshake_Artifacts/WP-KERNEL-STUDIO/smb-type-character-attributes-1/smb-type-character-attributes-1-red-e2f70907.log:64 (the folio test failed to compile on its own recursion limit); ...-focused-51b4d006.log:35119-35120; crates/hsk-studio-harness/tests/layout_character_attributes.rs:128, :178, :194-201; crates/hsk-studio-layout/tests/character_override_edits.rs (insert at byte 0, story never validated); brief topic proof (bundled run list)

answers.empty_story_form: Holds. tiles() (story.rs:171) skips only entry 0 when the stream is empty and that entry is [0, 0). A second [0, 0) entry fails end <= start, any entry with bytes fails end > len, and a non-empty stream behaves as before. The skipped entry's style reference, scope (check_story_style_scopes) and paragraph_direction are still checked, because those loops run over every entry. A file without a paragraph still validates (test), and replace_story_text splits it on the first edit (empty_story_edits). The round trip is exact: serde writes the [0, 0) paragraph with its style as stored, and the harness test reopens it as (0, 0, style). The removed session workaround validated a stripped copy but stored the engine form, so files written before the lane open unchanged. One behaviour moved: an empty paragraph without paragraph_direction in an 'unknown'-direction story was hidden by the workaround and is now refused. No writer found creates 'unknown' (layout_ui.rs:1003, idml_longdoc.rs:374 and toc.rs:144 all write left_to_right). No hostile empty form was found that opens and then misbehaves.
answers.override_shifting: map_pos rules: a position before the edit stays; a position at or after the edit's end moves by the length change; a position inside the deleted bytes goes to the edit start. Consequences: text typed at an override's first byte stays outside it and joins the span before; text typed at its last byte joins it; retyping exactly the override's bytes keeps the override; a replace that starts before an override extends the override over the replacement (the same as character ranges); deleting all of it drops it. Shifting is monotone, so overrides never come to overlap, but equal neighbours left by a delete are not merged (canonical again after the next set). UTF-8 has no surrogate pairs. Lone-surrogate JSON is a decode refusal, and UTF-16 offsets that split a character are refused invalid_input by byte_span. An override may split a base from its combining mark (allowed, then shaped apart; see F5). CR LF: F11. Gaps: F9 (no story cross-check), F10 (whole-content writers).
answers.script_runs: Correct for its stated rule. Common and Inherited characters join the current run (leading ones join the first), so marks never start a run. A text with no strong character is Zyyy, which the host declares Latn. Bidi is resolved by Type over the whole paragraph, so cutting styles per run does not change embedding levels. Type's vendored profile accepts only Latn, Arab, Hani and Zyyy (validate.rs:178, engine.rs:361-368). Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew and kana refused before the lane (declared Latn, then resolved_script failed) and are still refused (declared, then validate fails), so there is no regression; Arabic and Han now shape. Runs add span cuts (F1). Paired brackets and Han with kana are named gaps.
answers.stored_not_drawn: PDF: character_of reports each stored, non-default field it does not draw as character_attribute_not_rendered with a span count (scales, rotation, skew, aki, tsume, stroke weight, anti-aliasing, alignment, alternate forms, baseline direction and option, digits_type, the true booleans, underline and strikethrough of a drawing type, hyperlink, optical kerning, an unsynthesisable position), plus applied_language_unresolved. Silent losses: inert OpenType features and the case projections that use them (F4), unmappable case characters (F4), the text layer under case mapping (F2), the per-paragraph leading approximation, and RTL direction (F12). IDML: character_idml_loss reports one Unsupported entry per record kind that holds anything (style_character, character_overrides, stroke_styles, languages), with counts. Nothing is written into IDML, and nothing is dropped unreported.
answers.stroke_style_delete: Refused stroke_style_in_use while any style_character record or local override names the style in underline or strikethrough. Those are the only referrers today (paragraph rules and borders are not built). Built-ins and unknown names refuse unknown_stroke_style. Redefining a style in use keeps its references valid. The success path (delete, undo, redo) is untested (F15).
answers.language_after_delete: No language deletion row exists (cut), so a record cannot disappear under its ranges through this lane. Ranges keep the key string. A key with no record (older or foreign files) shapes as the key when it parses as a locale, else as und, and is reported applied_language_unresolved. Redefining a record keeps its name. The domain mismatch between record names and range keys is F7.
answers.undo: All six mutating rows go through LayoutEditor::apply, which pushes the whole previous LayoutDoc and records, and Viewer::layout_apply commits one session step named by command_id(). A session refusal undoes the editor. Undo and redo are exact snapshot swaps. The harness test proves the six labels in order and one live undo.
answers.host_integration: Typed refusals: unknown_story, unknown_style, invalid_input (span), unknown_stroke_style, stroke_style_in_use, unknown_language, unknown_character_attribute, folio_<code> with the record target, and decode refusals from folio_field!. Undo names are the catalog ids (LayoutEdit::command_id, layout_ui.rs:227-235). Attribution comes from the caller's context through layout_commit and Run::submit_layout (the test checks the step's actor). The read row is mutates=false. clear is bounded (MAX_CLEAR). No new GPU, egui or job code. The export keeps the existing JobPort admission.
answers.spec_ranges: The numeric rows equal the STU-TYP-155, 158 and 159 tables: UNKNOWN stays None; defaults tracking 0, kerning_manual 0, scales 100, shift, rotation and skew 0; stroke_weight hard_min 0; synthesis 1..200, 0..200 and -500..500; tints 0..100; tracking and kerning_manual at precision 0, enforced as whole numbers. The enumerations match STU-TYP-156 and 133 member for member. Deviations: positive-only domains that the rows do not state, missing steps, binary features stored as integers (F13). STU-TYP-174 second storage for overlap_swash, stretched_alternate and kana (lead question 4). metrics_roman_only turns kerning off for every non-Latin run, including Arabic (lead question 6).
